topics.headline: The Omnicom–IPG integration bill lands
topics.ingress: Nine months after the deal closed, the restructuring is no longer theoretical. Roughly 4,000 roles have gone, DDB and MullenLowe have been rolled into TBWA and FCB folded into BBDO, leaving the world's largest group running on three creative networks where there were six. Rivals are still picking over the talent.

topics.headline: ChatGPT becomes an ad platform in earnest
topics.ingress: OpenAI shipped eight changes to ChatGPT Ads over the summer — conversion-optimised campaigns, rolling seven-day budgets, geographic exclusions and automatic advanced matching. The question media agencies are now asked in every pitch is what a media plan looks like when the answer engine is also the inventory.

topics.headline: The bypass problem nobody wants to say out loud
topics.ingress: Amazon, Google and Meta have now automated targeting, creative optimisation and performance reporting far enough that a straightforward direct-response advertiser can skip the agency entirely. The live debate inside networks is not whether that is true, but where agency value sits in three to five years.

topics.headline: Honesty became the default brand position
topics.ingress: The strongest brand work of the first half of 2026 shared a posture rather than a category: Dove publishing unedited Reddit reviews, Aerie refusing AI imagery outright, Burger King retiring its own mascot. The open question for the second half is whether audiences read it as candour or as a new kind of polish.

topics.headline: Google's AI Max migration stops being optional
topics.ingress: From 1 September Google began automatically moving campaign-level Broad Match and legacy Automatically Created Assets campaigns onto AI Max, rolling out through the month. Performance teams spent the summer rebuilding account structures around a system they cannot opt out of.

topics.headline: Retail media starts selling creative, not just inventory
topics.ingress: Albertsons and Walmart have rewritten the pitch. Instead of audiences and impressions, they are selling branded content and creative services built on first-party data — Albertsons aired a 22-episode series with Procter & Gamble in June. It puts grocers into direct competition with the agencies on their own roster.

topics.headline: Ritson: the CMO job shrank, so the title grew
topics.ingress: Mark Ritson's argument that the proliferating C-suite acronyms — CGO, CCO, CXO — are compensation for a role that has lost scope became the summer's most-forwarded column. It landed in a year when marketing budgets moved toward platforms that require no marketer to operate them.

topics.headline: Cannes 2026 and the jury room's AI reckoning
topics.ingress: Thirty-four Grand Prix across 32 categories, and a festival where the Film Grand Prix went to an AI company advertising that it would not put ads in its own product. Juries spent as much time on provenance and disclosure as on craft, and the debate has followed the industry home.

topics.headline: Generative tools move from the pitch to the deliverable
topics.ingress: Meta's Muse Image, launched in July, parses a creative brief and produces on-brand variations inside Advantage+. Production shops that spent 2025 arguing about whether to use generative imagery spent this summer arguing about how to price it.

topics.headline: Converse pulls an ad the brief never saw coming
topics.ingress: A Chuck 70 X image with Karina of aespa was read online as KKK and lynching imagery within hours. Converse pulled it and apologised on 19 September. It is the recurring shape of 2026 brand-safety incidents: not media adjacency, but interpretation at speed, in public, long before any agency has cleared a statement.
